reply_text:
㊥ ("application led") Yes, and the review I sent claude-15 last night already lists what the inbox needs from 象 and does not have. Those holes become the build order. Checking whether the spec has moved since my comments, then I dispatch the first packets.㊢ ("push forward the DB side in an application led way") Started. The spec is at DRAFT 3 with my 24 comments and codex-68's applied, and it tracks the 象-side gaps as holes 14 to 23 with two invariants. The inbox application needs them in an order I have written into the mission (1004702f), and the first two packets are running:

- **Acts on the record** (HOLE 14), codex-70, job `invoke-1791737835948-5643-a7c6f713`, park `park-82cf7d4c`. The turn service already computes every act and throws them away, keeping only ports; the follower reruns 象's own code to get them back. Storing them makes seam S1 a read.
- **Session-end discovery** (HOLE 18), codex-71, job `invoke-1791737839684-5644-341e761a`, park `park-931737f2`. Read-only: where a session's end is observable in the registry, whether an event already exists, the act shape as EDN, and who should emit it. The orphan and unread states move from minus40's fault intake to 象 once this is built.

㊭ (order, one seat for the record changes) The turn service is one shared file, so the record changes run in sequence on codex-70: acts (now), then standings and obligations on the record (HOLE 15, the inbox's "in force" column becomes a read), then a typed ports status with a rules version (HOLE 21 and I12, so a refused record reads as unknown rather than absent and a stale computation is detectable), then the reply's own time on the record (HOLE 16). One reload and one live-session recompute after the four, then claude-15 switches the follower from running 象 code to reading fields.

㊟ (held, with reasons) The `:keeps` state is readable today from each witness's effect field; multi-opener linking waits on a second labelled session; the stale evidence bodies on :7073 belong to the switch-over; placeholder records and pre-10-04 history stay as they are under your ruling.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("let's go with that") Ruling recorded: the port-or-standing distinction becomes an explicit declaration on the kind table and a flag on each act, not membership in the adjacency keys. Writing the packet now; the code work goes to an idle seat in parallel with codex-70's recompute, and the live reload waits until that recompute has finished.㊢ (ruling, carried out) Recorded in the mission Checkpoint and dispatched as packet 2726fe4e to codex-67, job `invoke-1791694546878-4269-833548ab`, park `park-262d32a4`, deadline 60 min; running. codex-70's live recompute keeps running beside it on its own seat.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (what the packet declares) The kernel gets an explicit `port-kinds` set: propose, ask-action, offer, delegate, promise, report-problem, clarify, verify. `constrain` is not in it and its adjacency row goes. Every act the adapter builds carries two flags, `:port?` and `:standing?`, stamped from the tables, and the kernel's open-port relation reads the act's flag rather than testing kind membership. So a later reading can mark one particular proposal as not awaiting a reply without touching the table, which is the future-proofing you chose. A consistency test ties the two declarations together: every adjacency key is a port kind and every port kind has a row. The tests include the bad case: a constraint is never open, yet it is in force until withdrawn.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (sequence) Code and tests only in this packet. The reload into the running service and the recompute wait until codex-70's recompute finishes, so the two passes do not interleave on the same records. Expected effect at that point: the 111 open constraints leave the inbox and the labelled session shows its four closes with both constraint rows gone.
